Export & stickers

Any avatar can be rendered to a file: animated, still, or a whole set of stickers. Frames are drawn offline from a copy of the avatar's simulation, so exporting never stutters the live one, and the exporter's code loads only when you first use it.

bot.export()#

const gif = await bot.export({ format: 'gif', duration: 2.4, fps: 20 });
const url = URL.createObjectURL(gif);
OptionValuesDefault
formatgif, apng, webm, sprite (a sheet of frames), png, webpgif
durationseconds of animation2 (WebM 3)
fpsframes per second20 GIF, 25 APNG and sprites, 30 WebM
scalepixels per CSS pixel2
backgrounda colour, or leave out for transparencytransparent

It resolves to a Blob; a sprite sheet's blob also carries blob.sprite (columns, rows, frames, frameSize, fps). WebM needs MediaRecorder; the others work everywhere the avatar does.

A still frame#

const png = bot.toDataURL({ scale: 4 });   // the current frame, synchronously

Stickers#

A single die-cut sticker (512px, white outline, transparent background), or a whole crew as a ZIP of stickers with a crew.json of names and DNA codes:

const sticker = await bot.export({ format: 'sticker' });          // PNG; frames: true for an animated APNG

import { exportStickers } from '@kucukkanat/bots/export';
const zip = await exportStickers([bot, { type: 'cat', hat: 'party', label: 'Mia' }, 'bot1.…'], {
  size: 512, outline: true,
});

The list takes live avatars, option objects or DNA codes (any other string is used as an identity). Use them as reactions in Slack or Discord, or as a WhatsApp or Telegram sticker pack.

In the studio#

The studio exports the bot you're designing as GIF, APNG, WebM or a sprite sheet with one click, no code.
